Hi Tom — great to meet you and the Acme team yesterday. Appreciate the eval file, that helped. Below is a concise post-demo recap and our recommended shortlist + rationale. I've attached the prompt set and our model profiles PDF for your architects.

Recap (quick):
- Use cases: customer-facing chat (low-latency, high throughput) + long-form summarization (higher quality tolerable).
- Latency target: P95 < 300ms for chat; Summarization can tolerate longer.
- Data: internal docs + user queries; no regulated PII in this project (for now) — flagged if that changes.

Recommended model shortlist (2 tiers):
1) "redwood-xl-1.0" (best quality/latency balance)
   - Rationale: strong long-form coherence, good end-to-end latency on A100-family GPUs, minimal quality regression risk vs. your baseline.
   - Tradeoffs: higher per-token cost than smallest models but lower hallucination rate for summarization.
2) "redwood-medium-quant" (cost-optimized variant)
   - Rationale: 4-bit quantized variant optimized for chat throughput; best cost/latency at scale with modest quality delta.
3) "redwood-compact-2" (fallback & cheap embedding service)
   - Rationale: very low cost for embeddings and short-turn exchanges; use as a degraded fallback for burst traffic.

Links and artifacts:
- Eval dashboard: https://redwood.app/dashboards/acme-evals
- Prompt set used in demo: attached (prompt_set_acme.txt)
- Model performance profiles: attached (redwood_model_profiles.pdf)

Next steps (proposed):
- Technical deep-dive with Neha + Marcus to map token budgets, batching, and KV cache strategy (30–45m).
- Provide sample doc set and a few production queries for a targeted eval (Neha will lead).
- Commercial: I'll share an indicative pricing sheet and can propose a dedicated commit if you want predictable latency/cost.

Available times: Tue 3/3 10–11am PT or Wed 3/4 2–3pm PT. Which works?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Tom / Marissa — jumping in with the SE perspective and a short technical plan.

TL;DR: For your P95 <300ms chat SLO we recommend testing redwood-medium-quant with the following config: 8-token prefetch KV cache, batch target 4–8 reqs, and fast-fallback policy to redwood-compact-2 for bursts. For summarization use redwood-xl-1.0 with a 16k context and n=1 sampling.

What I need from Acme to run a targeted eval:
- 500 anonymized user queries representative of chat traffic (or a sampling of logs).
- 200 long-form documents and example summarization prompts.

Planned eval deliverables (1 week turnaround):
- Token-level cost estimates per model and per-request latency P50/P95.
- Quality: ROUGE / BLEU / human rating samples for summarization.
- Failure modes: common hallucination cases and mitigation (system prompts, verify step).

Note on quantized models: redwood-medium-quant reduces cost ~3–4x vs. full precision on similar hardware but can increase extraction hallucinations in niche domains; we'll include tuned prompt templates to mitigate.

Sending a small prompt sample attached to illustrate the scoring harness.

—Neha
